integrity: The two leaves of a half graph force strong lower-bound constraints under the quasi-total Italian rule. At weight four, any departure from the two extreme universal defenders either leaves an internal zero with less than two units in its nested neighborhood or leaves a label-2 vertex unsupported. This proves uniqueness for n at least four; the two smaller half graphs are handled by finite exact case analysis. The quasi-total strong differential follows from the published Gallai identity.
scientific_limitations: The theorem classifies minimum quasi-total Italian functions rather than all feasible higher-weight functions.
The boundary cases n=2 and n=3 have exceptional optimizer multiplicities.
Finite exhaustive verification through n=7 is corroborative only.
A differently phrased or non-indexed half-graph result may exist.
title: Minimum quasi-total Italian functions of half graphs
